The Bayes' theorem update (primitive 1) serves as the foundational inference engine, enabling traders and agents to revise their strategies based on streaming data. However, this requires a robust feature extraction pipeline (primitive 2) to generate informative inputs for the model. Loss probability (primitive 3) complements win probability by framing risk management explicitly. The underlying computer architecture (primitive 4) provides the hardware substrate necessary to execute these algorithms at scale without unacceptable latency. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop predictive control system where uncertainty quantification drives decision-making. Failure modes include model drift due to non-stationary environments, over-reliance on historical patterns, and computational bottlenecks during peak load. To mitigate, conformal prediction techniques can be integrated to provide finite-sample coverage guarantees, while GPU-accelerated sampling methods address scalability demands.
